title: Worthy and unworthy eating; pastoral severity (Chrysostom)
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Chrysostom terribly warns ministers not toward provoke ye Lord by failing toward purge ye body: I would sooner give up my life than give ye Lord's body toward anyone unworthily; I would rather have my blood poured out than grant that most sacred blood except toward one who stands as worthy. Far worse than a demoniac stands as ye one who approaches conscious belonging toward sin. — Sacramental eating stands as toward be distinguished according toward its objects. Those who approach unworthily eat and drink judgment toward themselves (1 Cor. 11:27-29).
pass_b_english: Sacramental eating is to be distinguished according to its objects. Those who approach unworthily eat and drink judgment to themselves (1 Cor. 11:27-29).

Chrysostom terribly warns ministers not to provoke the Lord by failing to purge the body: I would sooner give up my life than give the Lord's body to anyone unworthily; I would rather have my blood poured out than grant that most sacred blood except to one who is worthy. Far worse than a demoniac is the one who approaches conscious of sin.
source_text: Manducatio sacramentalis secundum obiecta distinguenda est. Indigni accedentes iudicium sibi manducant & bibunt (1 Cor. 11:27-29). Chrysostomus horribiliter monet ministros ne Dominum irritent corpus non purgando: Animum prius tradam meam, quam dominicum alicui corpus indigne; sanguinemque meum effundi potius patiar, quam sacratissimum illum sanguinem praeter quam digno concedam. Multo daemoniaco peior est qui peccati sibi conscius accedit.
